label: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-8P-2G-L
description: Cisco Catalyst 1000 C1000-8P-2G-L - 8x 1G RJ-45 all PoE+ (802.3af/at, 30 W a port, 67 W budget), 2 combo uplinks that are 1G SFP or 1G RJ-45, one of the two at a time, 20 Gbps switching bandwidth, 14.88 Mpps at 64 bytes, fanless 1U Cisco IOS L2 access switch.

poe.note: 67 W PoE budget across 8 PoE+ ports, IEEE 802.3af/802.3at PSE, 30 W maximum a port. Perpetual PoE holds power on the PD across a reload. The budget, not the port count, is the ceiling: 4 Class-3 (15.4 W) PDs or 2 30 W PDs fit (4 x 15.4 W = 61.6 W, 2 x 30 W = 60 W).

notes: Datasheet Table 1 and Table 2: 8 copper ports, 2 combo uplinks that are 1G SFP or 1G RJ-45, one of the two at a time, 67 W PoE budget, fanless, 10.56 x 12.73 x 1.73 in deep, 1.55 kg; single internal autoranging 100-240 VAC supply; 14.88 Mpps forwarding rate; 16,000 unicast MAC entries, 256 active VLANs, 4094 VLAN IDs, 64 STP instances, 9198-byte L3 MTU, 10,240-byte jumbo frame. The switching bandwidth is the sum of every port at line rate, so no port group is oversubscribed. RJ-45 console (EIA/TIA-232) at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, no flow control; a USB Type A port takes a FAT-formatted flash drive for image and configuration recovery. Cisco calls the series Layer 2, but Table 2 budgets 542 IPv4 direct and 256 indirect routes (414/128 for IPv6), so static inter-VLAN routing is modelled as l3-forward, not a full L3 feature set. No 802.3bt anywhere in the series: 30 W a port is the ceiling. The 8P-2G-L is the deeper chassis of the pair (12.73 in deep against the -E variant 7.28 in) because the PoE supply sits inside. The chassis is fanless, so the PoE budget is also a thermal limit.

notes: Datasheet Table 1 and Table 2: 24 copper ports, 4x 10G SFP+ uplink cages that also take a 1G SFP, 370 W PoE budget, one fan, 34.8 dB sound pressure, 17.48 x 13.59 x 1.73 in deep, 4.6 kg; single internal autoranging 100-240 VAC supply; 95.23 Mpps forwarding rate; 16,000 unicast MAC entries, 256 active VLANs, 4094 VLAN IDs, 64 STP instances, 9198-byte L3 MTU, 10,240-byte jumbo frame. The switching bandwidth is the sum of every port at line rate, so no port group is oversubscribed. RJ-45 console (EIA/TIA-232) at 9600 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, no flow control; a USB Type A port takes a FAT-formatted flash drive for image and configuration recovery. Cisco calls the series Layer 2, but Table 2 budgets 542 IPv4 direct and 256 indirect routes (414/128 for IPv6), so static inter-VLAN routing is modelled as l3-forward, not a full L3 feature set. No 802.3bt anywhere in the series: 30 W a port is the ceiling. The four uplink cages are SFP+ and take a 1G SFP as well as a 10G module. The 128 Gbps switching figure covers a 10G module in all four cages; with 1G modules it is 56 Gbps, as on the -4G models.
